projects.title: Development of Autonomous Objectives in Intelligent Systems

review.alternative: Goals may simply be hardcoded or retrieved from static dictionaries rather than dynamically formulated.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence showing that hierarchical strategies fail to improve goal prediction or preference elicitation in non-trivial environments.

claims.statement: Hierarchical planning models such as BIHRL allow agents to structure preferences and goals effectively in complex environments.

support.explanation: Demonstrates the efficacy of hierarchical planning structures in goal and value inference.
support.passage: We describe the Bayesian Inverse Hierarchical RL (BIHRL) algorithm for inferring the values of hierarchical planners, and use an illustrative toy model to show that BIHRL retains accuracy where standard BIRL fails.

actions.findings: Hierarchical planning models such as BIHRL allow agents to structure preferences and goals effectively in complex environments. [source-80d47fc1443b41fd]
actions.limitations: The initial analysis is based on preliminary source material and requires deeper empirical testing on open-ended information gain.
actions.next_questions: How do hierarchical inverse reinforcement learning models scale to open-ended inquiry?
actions.reason: Synthesizing collected evidence to establish a provisional notebook for autonomous inquiry.
actions.summary: This provisional notebook explores how an intelligence can formulate questions and pursue problem selection independently using hierarchical planning models and information gain concepts.
actions.title: Foundations of Autonomous Problem Formulation

proposal.summary: This cycle evaluates the foundations of autonomous problem formulation and inquiry without external instruction, utilizing collected literature and maintaining rigorous adherence to WAKE governance.
